identity.kind: used four-cylinder petrol car engine (seller says Toyota Camry old model)
read_from: photo 0 engine shape: inline four with distributor-style plug leads; no maker mark or engine code readable

claims.evidence: No Toyota mark or engine code is readable in photo 0; the layout is consistent with an older Camry four-cylinder but does not prove it.
The engine code stamped on the block is not shown.
Spark plug leads suggest an older design, but the exact engine is not readable.
Origin cannot be shown by a photo.

risks.risk: The engine may not be the Camry engine claimed; engine codes differ in value and fit.
risks.proof: Sharp close-up of the engine code and number stamped on the block.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced; engine code needed first

risks.risk: Engine may knock, smoke, or have low compression.
risks.proof: Clip of the engine running on a test stand or in a car, with sound, from cold start, with the seller's handwritten note in shot.

risks.risk: Cracked block or head, or oil mixed with coolant.
risks.proof: Photos of the block sides and underside and of the oil on the dipstick.

risks.risk: Accessories (alternator, starter, sensors, wiring) may be missing.
risks.proof: Photos of all four sides of the engine showing what is attached.

proof_requests: Sharp close-up of the engine code stamped on the block.
Clip of the engine running with sound, with a handwritten note showing today's date.
Photos of all four sides and the underside.
response.reason: It is clearly a used four-cylinder petrol engine, but no maker mark or engine code is readable, and the engine code is what sets the price, so the block stamp is needed before even a worst-case price.
